newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Monday were seen steady to $0.50 or possibly $1.00 per cwt higher amid outlooks for tight hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
Speculation that hot, humid weather this weekend in the Midwest would limit already light hog marketings further underpinned price projections, they said.
"There's not that many hogs out there. They'll have to raise bids to get the hogs," one central Indiana dealer said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen at $59.00-$59.50.
Illinois top hog prices to the plant expected $59.00 to $59.50, the livestock dealers said.
Indiana/Ohio prices for hogs at the plant were seen at a top of $59.50, they said.
Cash hog prices also were seen buoyed by a firm tone to pork values on Friday, the dealers said.

Fresh retail hams near midday Friday were quoted steady to $2.00 per cwt higher, pork bellies were $2.00 higher in a light test and lean trimmings $2.00 higher, USDA said in its central U.S. carlot pork report.
